rules.label: Contact pattern
rules.description: Which contacts change between the two models, and in which direction, over the whole receptor.
rules.tree_method: Ward linkage on the 20 leading principal axes of the unit-length vectors

rules.label: Intracellular side
rules.description: The same measure, restricted to contacts on the intracellular half of the helices, the intracellular loops and helix 8.
rules.tree_method: Ward linkage on the 20 leading principal axes of the unit-length vectors

rules.label: Extracellular side
rules.description: The same measure, restricted to contacts on the extracellular half of the helices and the extracellular loops.
rules.tree_method: Ward linkage on the 20 leading principal axes of the unit-length vectors

rules.label: Sequence
rules.description: Residue identity over the GPCRdb generic positions both receptors have.
rules.tree_method: Maximum-likelihood tree (FastTree 2.1.11; LG + CAT) over the GPCRdb generic residue positions, rooted at the midpoint; node height = largest distance down to a leaf

notes.similarity: Cosine similarity of the rule's vectors (signed, square-root damped dRRCS per contact pair between generic-numbered positions); share of identical residues for the sequence rule. 1 = the same, 0 = unrelated.
notes.similar: similar[i]: the 8 nearest receptors as [index, similarity under this rule, companion score, [[position, position, sign] ...]]. The companion score is sequence identity, or whole-receptor contact-pattern similarity for the sequence rule. The last item lists up to 3 contact pairs that contribute most (sign +1 stronger in the active model, -1 in the inactive model); empty for the sequence rule.
notes.links: A link joins two receptors that are each among the other's 3 nearest under the rule, unless the similarity is in the weakest quarter of best matches (link_floor).
notes.tree: merges: scipy linkage rows [a, b, height]; ids below n are receptors, id n + k is the cluster made by row k. Undo the last k - 1 merges to get k groups. order: leaf order. The sequence tree is also in atlas/sequence_tree.txt (Newick, branch lengths, support values on internal branches); tree_method says how it was made. Groups are browsing aids, not classifications.
